data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["RFC 9110 definitions are scoped to HTTP methods; log idempotency is a distributed systems property","RFC 9110 safe methods concern HTTP caching/proxying semantics; log operations have no such infrastructure concerns","RFC 9110 idempotency is per-method; log idempotency is per-operation-instance (identified by operation ID)"],"overturn_conditions":["If RFC 9110 explicitly states its definitions are general (not HTTP-specific), the category error argument collapses","If the question's intent is clearly analogical, refusing the analogy is unhelpful"],"shared_structure":["Both RFC 9110 idempotency and log-append idempotency share the mathematical structure f^n(x) = f(x)","Both concern the effect of operation repetition on system state"],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_002","SRC_006","SRC_007","SRC_008"],"transfer_claims":["The mathematical property f(f(x)) = f(x) transfers as a general principle from HTTP to distributed systems","The hierarchy 'safe implies idempotent' transfers as a general logical relationship"]},"claim":"The distinction per RFC 9110 is that safety forbids side effects while idempotency permits them but requires convergence under repetition. However, the append-only log does not require either property of its writers in the RFC 9110 sense \u2014 those definitions concern HTTP methods on resources. What the log actually requires is the distributed-systems property of *idempotent append semantics*, which is analogous to but not identical with RFC 9110 idempotency. The answer to 'which of the two properties' is idempotency, but the question itself contains a category error by mapping HTTP method semantics onto log writer behavior without acknowledging the scope mismatch.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If RFC 9110's definitions are interpreted as general (not HTTP-specific), the category error claim weakens and the answer simplifies to 'idempotency.'","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the question's framing is accepted as deliberately analogical rather than literal, the category error critique is pedantic and the straightforward 'idempotency' answer suffices.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If there exists an RFC or standard that explicitly defines safe/idempotent for log operations (not just HTTP), that definition supersedes the RFC 9110 analogy.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"RFC 9110 \u00a79.2.1\u20139.2.2 define safe and idempotent as properties of HTTP methods. These are not general-purpose distributed systems definitions. The question asks 'which of the two properties does an append-only event log require,' presupposing that one of the two RFC 9110 properties applies. In reality, the log requires a property that is *analogous* to idempotency (duplicate appends must not change log state) but is not defined by RFC 9110. The honest answer: the log requires idempotency in the general mathematical sense (f(f(x)) = f(x)), and RFC 9110's definition of idempotency is a specific instance of this general property. Safety is clearly inapplicable because appends have side effects.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
